info.title: MITK Workbench REST API
info.description:
REST API for MITK Workbench external process integration.
Enables Python scripts, web applications, and external tools
to interact with MITK Workbench via standard HTTP.

## Transfer Modes

Data endpoints support two transfer modes:
- **direct**: Binary data in HTTP body (`application/octet-stream`)
- **file-reference**: JSON with server file path (`application/json`)

The `X-MITK-Transfer-Mode` header takes precedence over the `Accept` header
when determining the response format for data endpoints.

## Property Scopes

Property endpoints support three scopes:
- **all**: Both node and data properties (default for GET)
- **node**: Only properties from the DataNode's property list (default for PUT/PATCH/DELETE)
- **data**: Only properties from the BaseData's property list

## Error Format

All errors follow RFC 9457 Problem Details format.

tags.name: Data
tags.description: Node data transfer (images, surfaces, point sets, etc.)

tags.name: Rendering
tags.description: Render window update and reinit operations

get.description: Returns health status of the REST API server and its dependencies.
Returns server info including version, capabilities, and DataStorage availability.

Returns the current file access configuration, including the mode and, when restrictions are active, the list of allowed directories. Clients can use this to discover which file paths are permitted for file-reference transfers.

Returns a paginated list of nodes from the DataStorage.
Supports filtering by hierarchy, path, data type, parent UID, and property values.
Supports sorting and field selection.

In addition to the declared parameters, any query parameter of the form `filter.{property}=value` is interpreted as a property-value filter on the node. The `{property}` part is the MITK property name. Supported operators on the value: exact match (`filter.visible=true`), inequality (`filter.visible!=true`), wildcard `*` (zero or more characters, e.g. `filter.name=CT*`), and wildcard `?` (exactly one character, e.g. `filter.name=Node_0?`). The optional `context` and `property_scope` parameters control how the property is looked up. See the user manual section 5.3 "Query Parameters" for the full filter contract -- the OpenAPI schema cannot model the dynamic `filter.{property}` family directly.

parameters.name: hierarchy
parameters.description: Filter by hierarchy level.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path-based lookup (e.g., "/CT_Scan" or "/Parent/Child"). May match multiple nodes when the path is ambiguous; the response is always an array (zero, one, or many entries) -- clients must not treat the single-match case specially.

parameters.name: data_type
parameters.description: Filter by MITK data class name (e.g., "Image", "Surface").

parameters.name: parent_uid
parameters.description: Filter by parent node UID. Use "null" for root nodes.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in response (e.g., "uid,name,data_type").

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order.
Example: `name` (ascending), `-timestamp` (descending).

post.description:
Creates a new top-level node in the DataStorage.

Supports two content types:
- `application/json`: Node metadata and optional file-reference transfer
- `application/octet-stream`: Direct binary data upload (name via query parameter)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Node name (used with `application/octet-stream` Content-Type).

schema.description: Binary data for the node. Requires Content-Disposition header with filename or X-MITK-Data-Format header.

failed_properties.description: Property keys that failed to deserialize

warning.description: Warning message (e.g., multiple data objects in file)

get.description: Returns a single node by its UID, including available property contexts.

available_contexts.description: Available property contexts for this node

patch.description:
Updates node metadata. Currently supports reparenting via the `parent_uid` field.
Set `parent_uid` to null to make a node top-level.

parent_uid.description: New parent node UID, or null for top-level

409.description: Reparenting would create a circular hierarchy reference

error.title: Circular Hierarchy Reference
error.message: Cannot reparent node: the target parent is a descendant of this node

delete.description:
Deletes a node from the DataStorage.
If the node has children and `recursive` is not set to true, returns 409 Conflict.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: If true, also delete all children recursively.

error.title: Node Has Children
error.message: Node has 3 children. Use ?recursive=true to delete.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of child nodes for the given parent node. Supports the same filtering and pagination as GET /datastorage/nodes, including the dynamic `filter.{property}=value` family with `*`/`?` wildcards and `!=` negation. See GET /datastorage/nodes (and user manual section 5.3) for the full filter contract.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path-based lookup within children. May match multiple nodes when the path is ambiguous; the response is always an array (zero, one, or many entries).

parameters.name: data_type
parameters.description: Filter by MITK data class name.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort field (prefix with `-` for descending).

post.description:
Creates a new node as a child of the specified parent node.
Same request format as POST /nodes.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Node name (used with `application/octet-stream` Content-Type).

get.description:
Downloads the data attached to a node (e.g., image, surface, point set).

Transfer mode is determined by:
1. `X-MITK-Transfer-Mode` header (takes precedence)
2. `Accept` header
3. Default: `direct` mode

**Direct mode**: Returns binary data with `application/octet-stream` content type.
**File-reference mode**: Returns JSON with a server file path.

404.description: Node not found or node has no data

error.title: Node Not Found
error.message: No node found with UID 'invalid-uid'

error.title: No Data
error.message: Node 'node_1' has no data attached

500.description: Internal server error or serialization failure

error.title: Internal Server Error
error.message: An unexpected error occurred

error.title: Serialization Error
error.message: Failed to serialize node data to temporary file

put.description:
Uploads or replaces the data on a node.

**Direct transfer** (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`):
Send binary data in the request body. Must provide filename via
`Content-Disposition` header or format via `X-MITK-Data-Format` header.

**File-reference** (`Content-Type: application/json`):
Send JSON with `transfer.file_path` pointing to a file on the server.

file_path.description: Path to file on the server

warning.description: Warning if file contained multiple data objects

422.description: File not found or read error

error.title: File Not Found
error.message: Referenced file path does not exist: /path/to/file.nrrd

fileReadError.summary: File exists but could not be read

error.title: File Read Error
error.message: Failed to read file: /path/to/file.nrrd

get.description: Returns all properties of a node, filtered by scope, context, and optional name list.

parameters.name: property_scope
parameters.description: Which properties to return. Default is `all` for GET.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Whether to include property values. Set to `false` for keys only.

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of specific property names to return.

put.description:
Replaces all properties on a node (PUT semantics).
Existing properties not in the request are removed (except protected properties).
Default scope is `node`.

parameters.name: property_scope
parameters.description: Which property list to replace. Default is `node` for PUT.

replaced.description: Names of properties whose values were written by this request.

removed.description: Names of properties that existed in the previous state but were absent from the request body and have been removed.

patch.description:
Updates multiple properties on a node (merge semantics).
Only specified properties are modified; others remain unchanged.
Default scope is `node`.

parameters.name: property_scope
parameters.description: Which property list to update. Default is `node` for PATCH.

get.description: Returns a single property value by key.

parameters.name: property_scope
parameters.description: Which property list to search. Default is `all` for GET.

error.title: Node Not Found
error.message: No node found with UID 'invalid-uid'

error.title: Property Not Found
error.message: Property 'nonexistent' not found on node 'node_1'

put.description:
Sets a single property value. Creates the property if it doesn't exist.
Default scope is `node`.

parameters.name: property_scope
parameters.description: Which property list to set on. Default is `node` for PUT.

replaced.description: True if the property existed before

delete.description:
Deletes a property from a node.
The `name` property is protected and cannot be deleted in node scope.
Default scope is `node`.

parameters.name: property_scope
parameters.description: Which property list to delete from. Default is `node` for DELETE.

400.description: Property is protected and cannot be deleted

error.title: Property Protected
error.message: Property 'name' cannot be deleted

post.description: Requests all registered render windows to be updated via `RenderingManager::RequestUpdateAll()`. Callers should use this after batching data or property changes to make them visible without triggering per-change flicker.

type.description: Which render windows to update: all, only 2D windows, or only 3D windows.

422.description: An unexpected error occurred in the rendering framework

error.title: Rendering Error
error.message: Rendering operation failed: ...

post.summary: Reinit -- fit all views to visible data or specific nodes
post.description: Three operating modes: (1) No body -- global reinit, fits all render windows to the bounding box of all currently visible data nodes via `RenderingManager::InitializeViewsByBoundingObjects()`. (2) Body with `uids` containing one UID -- single-node reinit, fits render windows to the geometry of that node. (3) Body with `uids` containing multiple UIDs -- multi-node reinit, fits render windows to the combined bounding geometry of all listed nodes. Both node cases use `RenderingManager::InitializeViews()`. Equivalent to clicking the global reinit button in the Workbench.

uids.description: When provided, fit views to the bounding geometry of the specified nodes. Use one UID for single-node reinit, multiple UIDs for multi-node reinit. Every listed node must exist and have a usable geometry.

422.description: A listed node has no data or the data has no usable geometry

error.title: No Data
error.message: Node 'node_1' has no data attached.

no-geometry.summary: Node data has no usable geometry

error.title: No Geometry
error.message: Node 'node_1' has no usable time geometry.

error.title: Rendering Error
error.message: Rendering operation failed: ...

get.summary: Get crosshair position and scene bounds
get.description: Returns the current crosshair position in world coordinates via IRenderWindowPart::GetSelectedPosition() on the StdMultiWidgetEditor, and the world-space AABB from the reinit geometry (TimeNavigationController input world time geometry). If no input geometry is available, bounds.min_position and bounds.max_position are null. Requires the Qt workbench plugin to be running (503 RENDER_WINDOW_NOT_AVAILABLE otherwise) and the StdMultiWidgetEditor to be open (503 EDITOR_NOT_ACTIVE otherwise).

200.description: Current crosshair position and scene bounds

position.description: Crosshair position in world coordinates [x, y, z]

min_position.description: World-space minimum corner of the scene AABB, or null if no geometry

max_position.description: World-space maximum corner of the scene AABB, or null if no geometry

put.description: Moves the crosshair to the given 3D world position via IRenderWindowPart::SetSelectedPosition() on the StdMultiWidgetEditor. Requires the Qt workbench plugin to be running (503 RENDER_WINDOW_NOT_AVAILABLE otherwise) and the StdMultiWidgetEditor to be open (503 EDITOR_NOT_ACTIVE otherwise).

position.description: New crosshair position in world coordinates [x, y, z]

get.description: Returns all known editor aliases with their current activity state. The alias list is always complete, even when no editor is open, so clients can discover available editors. Both the `stdmulti` and `mxn` aliases are probed live; `active` is `true` only when an editor instance is currently open in the workbench.

200.description: List of editor aliases and activity state

get.description: Returns metadata about the StdMultiWidget editor, including its current window names when the editor is open.

Returns the StdMultiWidget editor's render windows. Each item carries the window id (URL segment for sub-resources), its kind (2D or 3D), and (for 2D windows) the persisted `view_direction`. No `plane` field is reported -- under swivel mode the live plane is not guaranteed to match an anatomical one; read orientation from the window's /camera if needed.
Per-window summary. `kind` drives which sub-resources apply. `has_selected_slice` is false for the 3D window.

get.summary: Get camera state of a StdMultiWidget window
get.description: Returns the camera state of the addressed render window. 2D windows (axial/sagittal/coronal) include `parallel_scale` and omit `perspective_angle`; the 3D window does the inverse.

put.summary: Update camera state of a StdMultiWidget window
put.description: Partial update. Any subset of the applicable fields may be sent; unspecified fields are left unchanged. `standard_view` programs the underlying CameraController; explicit pose fields (`position`, `focal_point`, `view_up`) bypass it and write the raw vtkCamera, so combining the two would leave the controller's internal state inconsistent -- this combination is rejected with 400. `standard_view` may still be combined with `parallel_scale` or `perspective_angle`, which only adjust scale/angle. Unknown fields, 2D-only fields on the 3D window, 3D-only fields on 2D windows, unknown `standard_view` values, non-positive `parallel_scale`, and `perspective_angle` outside (0, 180) are rejected with 400. World coordinates are not range-checked. Only the addressed window is refreshed; coupled crosshair/slice updates on sibling 2D windows happen through their own UI events.

422.description: MITK rendering framework raised an error while applying the patch.

error.title: Rendering Error
error.message: Camera update failed: ...

get.summary: Get selected slice of a StdMultiWidget 2D window
get.description: Returns the currently selected step, the world position of the slice center, and the scene navigation bounds. Not applicable to the 3D window (returns 404 UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION). No `plane` field is reported -- under swivel mode or node-initialised geometry the live plane is not guaranteed to match an anatomical plane; read orientation from the window's /camera if needed. When no geometry is loaded, `bounds.min_position` and `bounds.max_position` serialize as `null`.

put.summary: Set selected slice of a StdMultiWidget 2D window
put.description: Accepts only `{"step": N}`. To move by world coordinates, use PUT /rendering/selected-position (StdMulti slices are coupled). Sending a `position` field returns 400 with a hint. Not applicable to the 3D window (returns 404 UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION). `step` is not range-checked -- out-of-range values are clamped/snapped by MITK.

400.description: Invalid body, missing/negative/non-integer step, unknown field, or a `position` field was supplied (not accepted for StdMulti -- use /rendering/selected-position).

error.title: Invalid Request
error.message: 'position' is not accepted on StdMulti selected-slice. Use PUT /rendering/selected-position to move by world coordinates.

422.description: MITK rendering framework raised an error while applying the step.

error.title: Rendering Error
error.message: Slice update failed: ...

get.summary: Get current time step and time bounds
get.description: Returns the active time step and time point from the global TimeNavigationController, together with the time geometry bounds.

min_timepoint_ms.description: Start of the time range in ms

max_timepoint_ms.description: End of the time range in ms

put.summary: Set active time step or time point
put.description: Sets the active time in the global TimeNavigationController. Exactly one of 'timepoint_ms' or 'timestep' must be provided.

422.description: Resolved time step is outside the available range [0, steps), or unexpected error in the rendering framework. Out-of-range inputs are rejected rather than silently clamped.

get.summary: Capture a screenshot of the active application window
get.description: Captures a screenshot of the active Qt application window. Requires the Qt workbench plugin to be running. Returns binary image data in PNG or JPEG format.

get.summary: Capture a screenshot of the StdMultiWidget editor canvas
get.description: Grabs the StdMultiWidget editor's canvas area (all four render windows together, no side panels). Query parameters and response contract are identical to `GET /rendering/screenshot`.

get.summary: Capture a screenshot of a single StdMultiWidget render window
get.description: Grabs a single render window without resizing the live render surface. If a different `width`/`height` is requested, the captured image is scaled after the fact, ignoring the source aspect ratio (i.e. stretched to fit) -- pass dimensions matching the source ratio if a faithful aspect is needed. Query parameters and response contract are identical to `GET /rendering/screenshot`.

Returns metadata about the MxN multi-widget editor, including its current cell ids when the editor is open. Cell ids are in the canonical fully-qualified form `<editor_name>__<bare>` (e.g. `mxn__widget0`), match the `id` field of each `window` leaf in the v2 layout document, and are used verbatim as the URL segment for sub-resources; no prefix translation happens at any boundary.

Returns the MxN editor's cells in pre-order traversal of the current layout. Each entry carries the cell `id` in the canonical fully-qualified form `<editor_name>__<bare>` (the same string used as the URL segment for sub-resources and as the layout document's `id` field), an optional human-readable `name` (display label, omitted when the cell has no display name set), the kind (always `2d` under v2; `3d` reserved for forward-compat), the persisted `view_direction` from the layout document, and the cell's `links` object. v2 has one link dimension (`selection`); v3 will add more dimension keys here additively without breaking v2 clients.

get.summary: Capture a screenshot of the MxN editor canvas
get.description: Grabs the MxN multi-widget canvas (the cell tree only -- no toolbars, no side panels). Query parameters and response contract are identical to `GET /rendering/screenshot`.

get.summary: Capture a screenshot of a single MxN cell
get.description: Grabs a single MxN cell render window without resizing the live render surface. If a different `width`/`height` is requested, the captured image is scaled after the fact, ignoring the source aspect ratio (i.e. stretched to fit). Query parameters and response contract are identical to `GET /rendering/screenshot`.

get.summary: Get the current MxN layout document
get.description: Returns the v2.0 layout document the editor would persist if asked to save right now. Always strict-mode: every group referenced by a cell appears in the top-level `groups` dict. The response body is byte-equivalent (modulo whitespace) to an in-tree `mxnLayout_*.json` preset file -- same schema, same shape (see `mxn-layout-v2.schema.json`).

schema.description: v2.0 layout document. Validated against `mxn-layout-v2.schema.json` (https://mitk.org/schemas/mxn-layout-2.0.json) -- see that file for the full field-level spec.

put.summary: Apply a v2.0 layout document to the MxN editor
put.description: Applies the supplied v2.0 layout document. **All existing cells are torn down and rebuilt from the document** (no positional reuse) -- any cell id a client cached prior to the PUT is invalid afterwards. The 200 response body is the freshly serialized layout (same shape as GET), so callers can refresh their cell list from the response without a follow-up GET. Schema and structural failures (version != 2.0, duplicate window ids, unknown view direction, missing group reference, type errors, ...) surface as `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with a precise `detail` message. The body is validated against `mxn-layout-v2.schema.json`.

200.description: Layout applied. The body is the freshly serialized layout (same shape as GET).

get.summary: Get camera state of an MxN cell
get.description: Returns the camera state of the addressed MxN cell. Under v2 every MxN cell is 2D, so the response carries `parallel_scale` and omits `perspective_angle` (mirrors the StdMulti 2D-window shape). When v3 introduces a 3D MxN cell type the response will switch to the 3D shape (`perspective_angle`); the schema is unchanged.

put.summary: Update camera state of an MxN cell
put.description: Partial update -- at least one camera field must be present. `standard_view` is applied first; explicit pose fields override its effect (cannot combine `standard_view` with `position`/`focal_point`/`view_up`). Under v2 every MxN cell is 2D, so `perspective_angle` is rejected with 400; `parallel_scale` is accepted. Field validation, unknown-field rejection, and the rest of the contract mirror the StdMulti camera PUT.

get.summary: Get the cell's currently selected slice
get.description: Returns the cell's selected-slice state: integer step plus the live world position on the slice plane plus navigator bounds. `bounds.min_position` / `bounds.max_position` are `null` when no geometry is loaded (mirrors the global selected-position bounds convention).

put.summary: Step the cell's slice navigator to a target index
put.description: Body: `{"step": N}` only. World-anchor moves on a single MxN cell live at the per-cell selected-position resource (`PUT .../selected-position`); global anchor moves at `PUT /rendering/selected-position`. Sending `position` here returns 400 with a hint pointing to both primitives. No range checking -- out-of-range step values are clamped/snapped by the navigator (D15).

get.summary: Get the per-cell 3D world anchor of an MxN cell
get.description: Returns the cell's selected position (3D world anchor) plus scene bounds. Same shape as `GET /rendering/selected-position` but per-cell-scoped -- distinct resource from the global one (D8). An unsynced MxN cell may legitimately have a different anchor than the global one. `bounds.min_position` / `bounds.max_position` are `null` when no geometry is loaded.

put.summary: Set the per-cell 3D world anchor of an MxN cell
put.description: Sets the cell's selected position. Distinct from the global `/rendering/selected-position` resource: this targets a single cell's anchor via `QmitkAbstractMultiWidget::SetSelectedPosition(point, widgetName)`. Whether the change visibly propagates to other cells (or to the global anchor) depends on the workbench's interactive coupling toolbar state -- that state is intentionally not exposed via REST. Clients that need a deterministic per-cell observation read each cell's `selected-position` after their PUT. No range checking -- out-of-range values are clamped/snapped by MITK (D15).

get.description: Per-cell summary. `view_direction` and `links` come from the layout document (persisted state, not live orientation). The optional `name` mirrors the layout document's display label and is omitted when the cell has no display name. Sub-resources: `/camera`, `/selected-slice` (2D cells), `/selected-position`, `/screenshot`. v2 has no 3D MxN cell type, so `has_selected_slice` is always `true`; the field is kept for forward-compat with future v3 cell types.

parent_uid.description: Parent node UID (null for top-level nodes)

data_type.description: MITK data class name (null if no data attached)

timestamp.description: ITK modified time (session-only counter, higher is newer)

documentation_url.description: URL of the REST API specification for the running MITK version. Released builds point to a version-specific path (e.g. /2026.06/); development builds (patch level 99) point to /nightly/.

uptime_seconds.description: Server uptime in seconds (omitted if unavailable)

restrictions_active.description: Whether file path restrictions are currently enforced

allowed_paths.description: List of allowed directory paths (only present when restrictions are active)

max_active_temp_dirs_per_ip.description: Maximum number of concurrently active file-reference temp directories per client IP. When a client exceeds this limit, its oldest directory is evicted automatically.

instance.description: Request path that caused the error

PropertyValue.description:
Property value. Simple types are returned as-is (boolean, number, string).
Complex types are returned as `{type, value}` objects.

properties.description: Initial properties to set on the node

transfer.description: Optional data transfer via file reference

file_path.description: Path to data file on the server
Path to the serialized data file

directory_path.description: Path to the directory containing all related files

returned_count.description: Number of items in this response

prev.description: URL for the previous page (absent if at start)

next.description: URL for the next page (absent if at end)

path_query.description: Path query applied (present only when path filter is used)

filters.description: Applied filters (present only when filters are active)

sort.description: Applied sort (present only when sort is active)

fields.description: Field selection (present only when fields parameter is used)

EditorListItem.description: Editor list entry returned by GET /rendering/editors.

alias.description: Stable short alias used in URL paths

active.description: True if an editor instance is currently open

windows.description: Current window identifiers (URL segments for sub-resources). For the MxN editor each entry matches the `id` field of the corresponding `window` leaf in the v2 layout document verbatim, i.e. the canonical fully-qualified form `<editor_name>__<bare>`. For StdMulti, the engine-fixed names (`axial`, `sagittal`, `coronal`, `3d`).

WindowListItem.description: Window list entry returned by GET /rendering/editors/stdmulti/windows. Convention: `view_direction` is present iff `kind == "2d"`; the StdMulti `3d` window omits it.

id.description: Render window id (engine-fixed slot token; URL segment for sub-resources). One of `axial`, `sagittal`, `coronal`, `3d`.

kind.description: Window kind -- drives which sub-resources apply

view_direction.description: Anatomical plane this slot renders. Present only for 2D windows; omitted for the 3D window. For StdMulti the value matches `id` by construction; the field is provided so generic clients can read `view_direction` uniformly across editor types.

WindowInfo.description: Per-window summary returned by GET /rendering/editors/stdmulti/windows/{id}. Convention: `view_direction` is present iff `kind == "2d"`; the StdMulti `3d` window omits it.

view_direction.description: Anatomical plane the slot renders. Present only for 2D windows; omitted for the 3D window.

has_selected_slice.description: True for 2D windows, false for the 3D window

MxNLinks.description: Per-cell synchronisation links from the layout document. v2.0 knows only the `selection` dimension; v3 will add more dimensions here additively (zoom, time, crosshair, ...). Tooling that reads the v2 shape continues to work in v3 unchanged.

selection.description: Group label for the selection bundle (selection list / stack order / visibility / select-all mode). Cells with the same value share the bundle at runtime.

MxNWindowListItem.description: Window list entry returned by GET /rendering/editors/mxn/windows. Carries the per-cell layout-document fields so REST clients don't need to fetch the full layout to know which cells exist. Convention: `view_direction` is present iff `kind == "2d"`. Under v2 only 2D cells exist, so `view_direction` is required; v3 will relax this when 3D cells are introduced.

id.description: Canonical fully-qualified MxN cell id (URL segment for sub-resources). Matches the `id` field of the corresponding `window` leaf in the layout document. URL-segment-safe and unique within the layout.

name.description: Optional human-readable display label. Mirrors the optional `name` field of the corresponding `window` leaf in the layout document. Free-form, not unique. Omitted when the cell has no display name set.

kind.description: Cell kind; always `2d` under v2 (the schema's `view_direction` enum has no `3d` value). `3d` is reserved for v3 forward-compat.

view_direction.description: Persisted view direction from the layout document. Authoring intent, not live orientation -- read live orientation from /camera if needed.

MxNWindowInfo.description: Per-cell summary returned by GET /rendering/editors/mxn/windows/{id}. Adds capability flags (`has_camera`, `has_selected_slice`, `has_selected_position`) on top of the list-entry fields. Convention: `view_direction` is present iff `kind == "2d"`. Under v2 only 2D cells exist, so `view_direction` is required; v3 will relax this when 3D cells are introduced.

id.description: Canonical fully-qualified MxN cell id. Matches the `id` field of the corresponding `window` leaf in the layout document.

name.description: Optional human-readable display label. Mirrors the optional `name` field of the corresponding `window` leaf in the layout document. Omitted when absent.

has_selected_slice.description: True for 2D cells; reserved for v3 3D cells.

has_selected_position.description: True for every MxN cell -- per-cell selected position is a v2 capability (distinct from the global /rendering/selected-position resource).

CameraState.description: Camera state of a single render window. 2D windows carry `parallel_scale`; the 3D window carries `perspective_angle`.

perspective_angle.description: Vertical FOV in degrees; 3D window only.

SliceState.description: Slice navigator state returned by GET .../selected-slice. `bounds.min_position` / `bounds.max_position` are null when no geometry is loaded.

position.description: World position on the live slice plane

CameraPatch.description: Partial camera update. At least one field must be present. `standard_view` is applied before any other field.

ScreenshotWidth.name: width
ScreenshotWidth.description: Output width in pixels. Must be provided together with 'height'.

ScreenshotHeight.name: height
ScreenshotHeight.description: Output height in pixels. Must be provided together with 'width'.

StdMultiWindowId.name: id
StdMultiWindowId.description: StdMultiWidget render window id (the engine-fixed slot token).

MxNWindowName.name: id
MxNWindowName.description: Canonical fully-qualified MxN cell id from the current layout document (`<editor_name>__<bare>`, unique within the layout). Matches the `id` field of the corresponding `window` leaf verbatim; the engine, the layout document, and the URL share one form, with no prefix translation at any boundary.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of results per page (1-1000).

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination.

PropertyScope.name: property_scope
PropertyScope.description:
Which properties to consider.
- `all`: Both node and data properties
- `node`: Only node properties
- `data`: Only data properties

Context.name: context
Context.description: Renderer context for property lookup (e.g., a specific render window name).

ContentDisposition.name: Content-Disposition
ContentDisposition.description:
Provides the filename for binary uploads so the server can determine the
file format from the extension (e.g., `.nrrd`, `.nii.gz`, `.stl`).
Format: `attachment; filename="<name>.<ext>"`

DataFormat.name: X-MITK-Data-Format
DataFormat.description:
File format extension (without leading dot) for binary uploads.
Alternative to providing a filename via Content-Disposition.
Examples: `nrrd`, `nii.gz`, `stl`, `vtp`

TransferMode.name: X-MITK-Transfer-Mode
TransferMode.description:
Transfer mode for data endpoints. Takes precedence over the Accept header.
- `direct`: Binary data in response body
- `file-reference`: JSON with server file path
